Synopsis:
Dialog for the wheel of fortune mini-game operated by Akabi - the djinni, destroyer of the worlds. Players can win random magical items with side effects or try to uncover the cheating djinni performs and win a grind prize, upsetting him (which results in you being sent to a jungle to be eaten by dinosaurs).

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_Circus_FortuneWheelWorker.json: Akabi is a boastful, world‑destroying djinni who runs the Wheel of Wonders at the circus — a gambling mini‑game that hands out random magic trinkets (often with nasty side effects). Off‑screen the circus is tense: a beloved performer named Dribbles has gone missing or been killed, Lucretious the ringmaster is frantic about restoring them, and other staff and patrons are anxious. The wheel is rigged — Akabi cheats — but players can attempt to expose or out‑cheat him and win the jackpot or a special “grind” prize; doing so infuriates Akabi and can provoke extreme punishments (including being banished to a dinosaur‑filled jungle). The provided lines reflect a player distracting and then claiming victory while Akabi alternates between pompous gloating and furious accusations of cheating.
- WYR_Circus_Merchant.json: You’re talking to Popper, a circus kobold merchant who hawks weird, magical, and clearly shady curios — he behaves like a dealer who’s thrilled with his own stock. Off‑screen there was a recent scuffle with the Dribbles (small clown‑adjacent creatures) and one of their hands ended up severed; the hand is now among Popper’s wares. Popper claims he “found” it by the clown man’s tent and is evasive about any real connection to the Dribbles, then immediately tries to sell the hand for an exorbitant price. The exchange is therefore a mix of smug posturing, obvious lying, and an opportunity for the player to haggle or call his bluff.
- WYR_Circus_Clown_PreShow.json: Dribbles the clown (actually a doppelganger who stole the identity of the famous clown) is on a stage with Buddy the dog beside him. A large crowd looks on. In this scene, Dribbles invites the player on the stage. Player can 1) approach the stage 2) tell a companion to get up on stage or 3) refuse - in which case a fan will volunteer. At the end of the scene, Buddy the dog attempts to sneak up on whoever is on stage and attacks.
- WYR_Circus_Clown.json: Main dialogue for the Dribbles the Clown, who in reality is a disguised doppelganger serving the Bhaalists. The player may trigger it by using stealth and approaching the stage from behind.
- WYR_Circus_Thug_02.json: Dialog with the thug - Dribbles-doppelganger associate. Stands near the animal cages. Probably just a one-liner.

context: Akabi is a boastful, world‑destroying djinni who runs the Wheel of Wonders at a tense circus where a beloved performer, Dribbles, has gone missing or been killed and staff (including ringmaster Lucretious) are on edge. The Wheel hands out random magical trinkets (often with nasty side effects) and is secretly rigged — players can either take a normal spin or try to expose/out‑cheat Akabi to win the jackpot or a special “grind” prize. The provided lines reflect a player distracting Akabi (in the examples, by farting) to force the wheel to land on the jackpot while Akabi alternates between pompous gloating and furious accusations of cheating. Successfully beating Akabi angers him greatly and can provoke extreme punishments (including banishment to a dinosaur‑filled jungle).
